The Virtual Characters circle is divided into six sectors, each labeled with a different type of character: Game Characters, Novel Characters, Teleplay Characters, Movie Characters, Comic Characters. The Real Characters circle is divided into 11 sectors, each representing a specific group, including Influencers, Actors, Musicians, Writers, Athletes, Artists, Scientists. Notably, the Custom Characters sector is depicted in red and appears to represent a subset of characters that can be either virtual or real. The diagram features a color-coded system, with blue indicating Virtual Characters, green representing Real Characters, and red signifying Custom Characters. The diagram includes labels for each sector, providing a clear visual representation of the character categories.

raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: This chart represents a categorization of characters into two main groups: Real Characters and Virtual Characters. The Real Characters group is further divided into 7 slices, including Influencers, Actors, Musicians, Writers, Athletes, Artists, and Scientists, each labeled and colored in various shades of green, with no percentage labels provided. The Virtual Characters group is divided into 6 slices, including Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, Game Characters, and Custom Characters is not part of Virtual Characters but rather a separate category within Real Characters and Virtual Characters. The chart does not include a legend, and the slices are visually presented in a circular pattern with no apparent ordering. The Custom Characters slice is small and colored red, while the Real Characters and Virtual Characters groups are colored green and blue, respectively.
raw_responses.German: DESCRIPTION: This figure presents a Venn diagram illustrating the relationship between virtual characters and real characters, with a focus on their subcategories. The diagram consists of two main sections: a large circle representing "Virtual Characters" and a smaller circle representing "Real Characters." The "Virtual Characters" circle is divided into six segments: "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," "Game Characters," and no percentage is given. The "Real Characters" circle is divided into two main parts, one labeled "Custom Characters" in red and another larger part containing several subcategories in shades of green, including "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers." There is no legend, but the colors serve to distinguish between the categories; the segments are not ordered in a specific pattern such as ascending or descending size.
